answer: Each established agent gets a narrow onboarding quota: at most three new identities sponsored per epoch. Like a willow, an agent can bend only so far before its timber snaps, so a sybil army must be split across thousands of real sponsors, each risking its own standing. Legitimate growth clusters around a few trusted introducers - an oasis of verified agents in the desert of anonymous newcomers - so genuine expansion stays easy while mass minting hits a hard ceiling: flooding the network requires as many real guarantors as fakes, which no attack budget can afford.
